summary.oneLiner: India's largest CNC machine-tool maker is supply-constrained (running >100% utilization) against a structurally growing, import-substituting demand base; the near-tripling of capacity (6,000 → 16,000 machines, live Sep-2026) is the central growth unlock, while the Huron/France export-control investigation is a contained, non-cash-drag overhang (₹67cr revenue deferred, not lost).

thesis (one-line): India's largest CNC machine-tool maker is supply-constrained (running >100% utilization) against a structurally growing, import-substituting demand base; the near-tripling of capacity (6,000 → 16,000 machines, live Sep-2026) is the central growth unlock, while the Huron/France export-control investigation is a contained, non-cash-drag overhang (₹67cr revenue deferred, not lost).
scorecard (q4fy26 & fy26): ORDER BOOK (31-Mar-2026): ₹4,732 cr (now "₹4,700+ cr"; healthy & growing). Execution timeline 18–20 months.
Net debt: ~₹850+ cr (up YoY): ~₹300cr of the increase from capacity-expansion capex; only ~₹45cr from working capital. Mgmt does not foresee further debt rise.

One-offs (CRITICAL): ₹67 cr consolidated revenue deferred (not written off) under POCM at Huron due to pending export licenses → also a ~₹40 cr EBITDA/margin hit (costs already incurred). Both revenue and the margin recover in future quarters once export licenses are received. No further reversals expected.
Units: Q4 = 1,760 machines; FY26 = 5,550 machines. FY26 avg realization ₹35.62 lakh/machine (lowest since listing — mix shift to entry/mid level).
guidance (critical — explicit): Margin: EBITDA margin to remain 25%+ at standalone/consolidated level steadily; even at full utilization of new capacity with avg machine price falling to ~₹30 lakh, margin stays ~25% ("will not go down below 25%"). Reiterated multiple times.

Volume: FY27 target ~8,000–9,000+ machines (vs 5,550 in FY26) once new capacity ramps (~+50% of incremental area utilized); long-run momentum maintained at 25–30% YoY. Expects 20–30% speed/output increase post-commissioning.
Order inflow: Robust pipeline; ramp from September onwards; FY26 intake ₹2,364 cr; Q4 intake ₹700cr+.
Capex/Capacity: Expansion from 6,000 → 16,000 machines (adding 10,000) on track, commercial ops Q2FY27 / September 2026.
Huron (France) standalone: FY27 to return to "normal level" of ₹300–350 cr (vs ₹248 cr FY26).
Pricing: RM up 2–3% in last 2 months; new prices raised from 1-May-2026 for new orders/customers (naturally hedged via long mfg cycle; existing contracts fixed-cost, not pass-through).
Cash flow: Turned positive this year (vs negative last year); expects robust, improving CFO QoQ as working-capital cycle shortens post new facility. Not quantified.
order book & pipeline: Outstanding order book: ₹4,732 cr (31-Mar-2026), execution 18–20 months.
By tier: ~40% high-end (above ₹2cr), ~60% entry-level (<₹50 lakh) + mid-level (₹50 lakh–₹2cr). Aerospace/defence largely high-end; auto & gen-engg mostly entry/mid.
A&D execution: FY26 executed >₹800 cr of aerospace & defence; ~75% executed from India (Jyoti's own tech, NOT Huron-dependent).
New orders this quarter from Europe incl. Ukraine (~6 machines, ~₹70cr — to be executed from Huron, needs licenses next year) and French government; plus India A&D orders.

EMS order book static at ₹700cr for ~1.5–2 years (Tata Electronics et al delaying as they optimize capacity; ISM-2 & component PLI could revive). Margins on this backlog expected to be better (prices linked to dollar terms).
segment detail: Aerospace & Defence: Largest, high-margin/high-end; structural multi-year tailwind (global re-arming — Europe, China, Turkey, Italy expanding). Tech now indigenous to Jyoti (not Huron-reliant); 75% executed from India.

Auto & auto-component + General engineering: Strongest near-term momentum / fastest order conversion; mostly entry/mid-level; rising automation demand (manpower shortage). India machine-tool consumption +20% CAGR over 3 yrs; imports surging (Jyoti can't capture due to capacity constraint).
EMS: Soft/delayed; awaiting client capex (Tata Electronics, ISM-2 component-mfg PLI). Capacity fully fungible to gen-engg/auto/dies if EMS lags.

Huron (France): FY26 revenue ₹248 cr (Q4 only ₹25 cr; ₹105cr intercompany to standalone — ~70% of Huron machine content sourced from India). FY27 target ₹300–350cr. Capacity expanded last year (first new-assembly dispatch ~Aug–Sep 2026).
growth / optionality: 16,000-machine capacity unlock (+167% units) is the core re-rating lever.
15,000+ India customer base (up from 14,000); MSME manufacturing base expanding.
Import-substitution: India machine-tool imports surging at +20% CAGR consumption — large untapped pipeline Jyoti currently cannot serve.
EMS optionality (Tata Electronics, ISM-2, component PLI) — currently dormant, upside if it converts.
Huron normalization + license clearance = recovery of deferred ₹67cr rev + ~₹40cr margin.
margins & cost: Standalone EBITDA margin strong: Q4 31.9%, FY26 28.9%. Consolidated 24.6% Q4 / 25.2% FY26 (dragged by ₹67cr reversal with sunk costs / negative operating leverage).
Floor guidance: 25%+ EBITDA margin sustainable even as avg realization falls toward ₹30 lakh.

Per-machine economics debated: realization fell to ₹35.62 lakh (FY26, lowest since listing); EBITDA/machine ~₹10.85 lakh vs ~₹13 lakh earlier — higher volume offset by lower realization/mix, but % margin defended.
Cost: fixed-cost contracts (not pass-through); naturally hedged by long mfg cycle + price hikes on new orders (1-May-2026); RM up 2–3%.
capex / expansion: India + Huron combined installed capacity currently 6,000 machines/yr → expanding to 16,000 (adding 10,000). Commercial ops Sep-2026 (Q2FY27), on schedule.
~₹300cr incremental debt incurred for this expansion in FY26.
People added over last ~1.5 years and being trained ahead of ramp; +25 people added at Huron mfg; Huron new facilities operational from Nov-2025.
capital allocation: Net debt ~₹850+cr: predominantly capex-driven (~₹300cr), minimal WC increase (~₹45cr). No further debt build expected; deleveraging via stronger cash flows post-ramp.
Cash flow turned positive YoY; targeting robust QoQ CFO. No dividend/buyback discussion on call.
Huron retained — explicitly NOT for sale despite drag.
risks: Huron export-control investigation (French authorities): alleged Russia re-export routing (2022–23), GM suspended (standard protocol). No conclusion; could run 2/3/5 years. ₹67cr rev + ~₹40cr margin deferred; risk it stays deferred longer than expected. Mgmt: machines "in queue for licenses," recovery sure but timing unknown; no material operational impact; 50+ EU companies under similar probes.
Capacity constraint capping near-term growth (>100% utilization; lost/unbooked orders unquantified).
EMS demand delay (Tata Electronics et al) — key segment dormant ~2 yrs.
Commodity/RM inflation (2–3% recent) on fixed-price contracts.
Working-capital intensity of high-end / longer-cycle orders.
Geopolitical/tariff/West Asia conflict — energy prices, supply chain, RM availability.
management tone: Confident and assertive, especially on India growth, 25%+ margin floor and capacity ramp. Defensive but consistent on Huron investigation — repeatedly reframing ₹67cr as "deferment, not write-off," denying any rerouting, refusing to quantify timeline. Candid that EMS is soft and that capacity constraint is costing unquantified order share. Declined to give precise FY27 machine numbers ("will tell in 3–4 months once capacity completes").
non-obvious insights: Q4 standalone and consolidated revenue both = ₹599cr purely because all Huron Q4 sales (₹25cr) were intercompany to standalone and eliminated → unusual artifact, flagged by an analyst vs reported P&L.
₹67cr reversal carried an outsized ~₹40cr margin hit (very high-margin Huron machines), so consolidated margin understated by a one-off.

Huron is largely an assembly/brand front — ~70% of Huron machine content is manufactured in India and shipped to France; 75% of A&D executed from India → tech/IP is now indigenous, de-risking the India A&D book from the Huron investigation.

20 yrs post-acquisition, Huron's own revenue is roughly flat-to-lower vs 2007 (~₹250cr), but it bootstrapped Jyoti from ₹50cr → ~₹2,000cr via tech/precision-mfg transfer — value was the capability, not Huron's standalone P&L.
EMS backlog (₹700cr) now more profitable to execute (dollar-linked pricing vs lower locked input costs).
challenges → beneficiaries: Surging Indian machine-tool imports + Jyoti's capacity constraint = clear import-substitution beneficiary once 16,000-machine capacity is live (✅ JYOTICNC itself).
Global A&D capex super-cycle (Europe/Turkey/Italy/China re-arming) = demand tailwind ⭐.
EMS/component-PLI revival (ISM-2, Tata Electronics) = optional upside beneficiary if it converts.
qoq log: Q4FY26 (this call): Order book ₹4,732cr (31-Mar-26); FY26 intake ₹2,364cr (Q4 ₹700cr+). Standalone FY26 rev ₹1,949cr (+20%), EBITDA 28.9%, PAT ₹391cr. Consol rev ₹599cr Q4 (after ₹67cr Huron deferral), EBITDA 24.6%, PAT ₹91cr. FY26 machines 5,550 (Q4 1,760); realization ₹35.62 lakh. Capacity 6,000→16,000, live Sep-2026. Net debt ~₹850cr (~₹300cr capex). Guidance: 25%+ margin floor; FY27 ~8,000–9,000 machines; Huron FY27 ₹300–350cr. Key overhang: French export-control probe (₹67cr rev + ~₹40cr margin deferred).

scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
